extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and investigators applying for NCCIH/NIH grants (including clinical investigators, small businesses, and grantees)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and resource summary for preparing and submitting grant applications and conducting NCCIH-funded clinical research, including eligible mechanisms, application resources, oversight, and compliance topics. Intended to help applicants align proposals with NCCIH priorities and NIH requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCCIH’s Funding Priorities and Research Focus
rubrics_metrics.description: NCCIH funds and conducts research to help answer important scientific and public health questions about complementary health approaches. NCCIH works to determine what is promising, what helps and why, what doesn’t work, and what is safe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with NCCIH priorities: focus on complementary and integrative health approaches, emphasize establishing what is promising/efficacious/safe, and address public health significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCCIH Funding Opportunities (search)
rubrics_metrics.description: Search for NCCIH-supported funding opportunities and Notices using keywords or grant types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the search tool and advanced search options to find appropriate funding opportunity announcements (FOAs) and notices relevant to your project type and stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Trial Notices of Funding Opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: These clinical trial notices of funding opportunities (formerly known as funding opportunity announcements or FOAs) will help to address gaps in current research and build a strong evidence base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applying for clinical-trial-related funding, select FOAs aimed at filling research gaps and strengthening the evidence base; ensure the trial design meets the scope described in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: What Will NCCIH Fund?
rubrics_metrics.description: How we prioritize areas of research and consider budget when awarding funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications should demonstrate alignment with NCCIH research priorities and be realistic and justified with respect to proposed budget and scope; priority-setting and budget considerations influence funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Grants and Contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains award mechanisms used to get research funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the award mechanism appropriate to the project (e.g., research project grants, training, contracts); follow mechanism-specific requirements and allowability rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Award Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: General descriptions of award mechanisms used to get research funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand distinctions among mechanisms (grants vs contracts, cooperative agreements, SBIR/STTR, etc.) and select the correct mechanism and application pathway for your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Business Research Grant Program (SBIR)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small businesses should follow SBIR-specific eligibility, scope, budget, and submission requirements when applying for NCCIH SBIR awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCCIH Clinical Research Toolbox
rubrics_metrics.description: Contains templates, sample forms, and information materials to assist clinical investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided templates and sample forms to prepare study documents (protocols, forms, consent language) and to align study materials with NCCIH expectations for clinical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical Study Oversight Levels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and plan for the appropriate level of clinical study oversight (monitoring, data safety oversight, etc.) required for the proposed study based on risk and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Application Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to policies, writing tips, deadlines, forms, and more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utilize the linked resources for policy compliance, application formatting, deadlines, and effective writing strategies; follow NIH and NCCIH application instructions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who Can Apply for Funding
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify applicant and institutional eligibility before preparing an application; ensure required institutional approvals and registrations are in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-writing Advice and Sample Applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult sample applications and advice to model structure, level of detail, and responsiveness to review criteria; use examples to improve clarity and competitiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preapplication Technical Assistance Webinars
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend webinars and preapplication assistance sessions to clarify FOA expectations, submission processes, and review criteria; use them to ask targeted questions about fit and scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigor and Reproducibility (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must address NIH requirements for scientific rigor, transparent reporting, consideration of biological variables, and reproducibility; include plans for authentication, randomization, blinding, and statistical approach as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact NCCIH Staff to Discuss Proposed Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact NCCIH staff to discuss proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage program officers and staff early to discuss fit with NCCIH priorities, appropriate FOAs, and application strategy; use staff feedback to refine scope and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Library for Researchers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instructional videos to learn about application processes, common pitfalls, and NIH/NCCIH policies and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural Products Clinical Trials Resource
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand U.S. Food and Drug Administration requirements for a clinical trial that will use a natural product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing trials involving natural products, follow FDA requirements and the NCCIH natural products resource to ensure regulatory compliance, product characterization, and safety monitoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Policies and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Important information and procedures for investigators who already have grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to NCCIH and NIH grantee policies post-award, including reporting, budgetary procedures, and compliance obligations; consult resources for award management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded Grants and Contracts (portfolio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of research and training grants funded for both new and ongoing research, with links to abstracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review awarded grants to understand funded topics, study designs, and scope; use the portfolio to benchmark competitiveness and alignment with NCCIH priorities.
